hinge question: Which part takes water in from the soil?
Which part holds the plant upright?
Which broad green part catches light?
misconception revealed: Confuses light capture with soil uptake.

hinge question: Which part can lead to seeds after pollination?
A label arrow points below the soil. Which part is it most likely to show?
expected answer: Roots; check its position on the diagram.
plausible wrong answer: Flower, because every part is a flower.
misconception revealed: Ignores position and structure in a labelled diagram.

hinge question: Can colour alone prove which plant part a picture shows?
expected answer: No; check shape and position too.
misconception revealed: Relies on colour alone, excluding varied plant forms.

hinge question: Which part first takes water from soil?
misconception revealed: Confuses absorption with use of transported water.

hinge question: What does a stem do with water?
What do leaves take in for photosynthesis?
misconception revealed: Confuses light capture with root uptake.

hinge question: What is one job of a flower?
A stem is cut off from roots. Which job is disrupted?
plausible wrong answer: Taking light in from the air.

hinge question: Are roots and stems doing the same job?
expected answer: No; roots absorb and stems transport.
plausible wrong answer: Yes; both absorb water from soil.

hinge question: Which of these is a plant growth need: light or loud music?
misconception revealed: Mistakes an optional stimulus for a growth requirement.

hinge question: Where does a plant get water for growth in the example?
expected answer: From water supplied to the roots.

hinge question: Which is a suitable growth condition: warmth or permanent freezing?
What do mineral nutrients help support?
misconception revealed: Treats one requirement as a replacement for another.

hinge question: Two similar plants get the same water, but only one gets light. What changed?
misconception revealed: Does not track the variable changed.

hinge question: Can one small comparison prove that all plants need exactly the same conditions?
expected answer: No; it tests one case under stated conditions.
plausible wrong answer: Yes; one comparison proves every plant.

hinge question: If testing water, what should differ between the two pots?
plausible wrong answer: The seed type and the light as well.

hinge question: Should both pots have the same kind of seed?
plausible wrong answer: No, any different seeds are fine.

hinge question: What would you measure over time?
expected answer: A stated growth measure such as height.
plausible wrong answer: How much you like the plant.

hinge question: What should happen to light during a water test?
expected answer: Keep it as similar as possible.
plausible wrong answer: Change it in only one pot.

hinge question: Does a plan to use the allotment prove a plant has grown there?
expected answer: No; observe and record real results later.
plausible wrong answer: Yes; planning is an observed result.
misconception revealed: Treats proposed practical work as evidence.

hinge question: One pot is watered and also kept in the dark. Can water alone explain a difference?
plausible wrong answer: Yes; water is the only cause.
misconception revealed: Claims cause when more than one condition changed.

hinge question: What starts a real plant-growth record?
expected answer: A dated observation of the actual plant.

hinge question: Which pair is easier to compare over time?
expected answer: The same measure on dated checks.

hinge question: If a plant does not grow, should you add a made-up number?
plausible wrong answer: Yes; make the chart look complete.

hinge question: What does an ICT photo record need?
expected answer: A date and plant or pot label without pupil data.
plausible wrong answer: A pupil name and an assumed outcome.
misconception revealed: Conflates evidence with personal data or assumption.

hinge question: Can a practice picture prove what happened to your real plant?
plausible wrong answer: Yes; all plants grow the same.
misconception revealed: Transfers simulated evidence to the real investigation.

hinge question: Why keep water and light checks consistent?
misconception revealed: Confuses a fair method with a guaranteed outcome.

hinge question: Where does soil water enter the plant?
Which part carries water up from roots?
What comes next in the main route: soil → roots → ?
Where can transported water reach?
Are downward arrows from leaves to soil a good model of uptake?
expected answer: No; main uptake is soil → roots → stem → leaves.
misconception revealed: Confuses rain direction with internal transport.

hinge question: If a stem is blocked, what part of the route is interrupted?
What happens when pollen reaches a stigma?
misconception revealed: Confuses pollen transfer with seed movement.

hinge question: What must follow successful pollen transfer before a seed can develop?
Which plant structure can become a seed after fertilisation?
When does seed dispersal occur?
A bee carries pollen. Has it made a mature seed already?
expected answer: No; fertilisation and development may follow.
plausible wrong answer: Yes; pollen transfer is the whole process.
misconception revealed: Treats pollination as completed seed formation.

hinge question: Does every pollen transfer guarantee a viable seed?
expected answer: No; later processes and conditions matter.
misconception revealed: Overstates a single stage as a guaranteed outcome.

hinge question: A seed forms after gametes join. Which process is this?
A strawberry runner grows a new plant without gamete fusion. Which process?
misconception revealed: Treats all new plants as seed reproduction.

hinge question: A potato tuber sprouts a new plant. Is a seed required for this route?
plausible wrong answer: Yes, every new plant needs a seed.

hinge question: What distinguishes a runner from a fertilised ovule?
expected answer: A runner forms a plant without fertilisation; the ovule follows fertilisation.

hinge question: Do all plants produced by gardeners come from seeds?
expected answer: No; runners and tubers can also form plants.
plausible wrong answer: Yes; every plant starts from a new seed.

hinge question: Why may offspring from runners resemble the parent closely?
expected answer: The route does not mix gametes from two parents.
plausible wrong answer: Because wind always selects identical seeds.

hinge question: Which seed feature suggests wind dispersal?
How could a hooked seed travel?
Which clue supports water dispersal?
expected answer: The seed floats and moves in water.
misconception revealed: Confuses water transport with self dispersal.

hinge question: What might a bursting dry pod do?
expected answer: Throw seeds away from the parent.

hinge question: A model seed flies farther with a fan. What changed?
Can one model flight distance predict every real seed journey?
expected answer: No; repeat fairly and state the model limit.

hinge question: Ice becomes liquid water. What change is this?
Liquid water becomes ice. What change is this?
misconception revealed: Confuses reversible state change with reaction.

hinge question: Sugar becomes invisible in water. Has it vanished?
Which example can be reversed by a change of state?
misconception revealed: Treats a chemical change as state change.

hinge question: How might dissolved salt be recovered?
expected answer: Remove the water by teacher-approved evaporation.
plausible wrong answer: Filter the solution with ordinary paper only.

hinge question: Does every colour change prove a new substance formed?
plausible wrong answer: Yes; colour alone proves a reaction.

hinge question: How can insoluble sand be separated from water?
misconception revealed: Chooses a method unrelated to insoluble solid separation.

hinge question: Will ordinary filter paper trap dissolved salt?
How could salt be recovered from its solution?
What can reverse the melting of wax?
misconception revealed: Does not match method to state change.

hinge question: Why do sand and salt need different recovery methods?
expected answer: Sand is insoluble; salt is dissolved.

hinge question: Should pupils heat a solution without the teacher practical controls?
What happens when water freezes then melts?
What does rusting form from iron?
What remains after paper burns?
expected answer: New materials such as ash and gases.
misconception revealed: Ignores evidence of a chemical change.

hinge question: Will warming a rusty gate simply turn rust back into iron?
misconception revealed: Treats rusting as a reversible state change.

hinge question: Can brown colour alone prove an object is rusting?
expected answer: No; consider material and other evidence.
plausible wrong answer: Yes; all brown marks are rust.

hinge question: Should a burning example be performed as an unsupervised pupil test?
plausible wrong answer: Yes; flame is needed to understand it.
misconception revealed: Assumes a hazardous practical is necessary.

hinge question: What is a stimulus in a control pathway?
expected answer: A change away from the regulated range.

hinge question: What detects a change before coordination?
How do hormones travel in the body?
What does negative feedback tend to do?
expected answer: Counter a change and move toward a regulated range.

hinge question: A model releases a hormone before detecting any change. What step is missing?
misconception revealed: Treats the pathway as an unordered list.

hinge question: Are all homeostatic pathways hormonal?
expected answer: No; this is one type of coordination.

hinge question: Blood glucose rises after a meal. Which hormone helps lower it?
Blood glucose falls below the usual range. Which hormone helps raise it?
Which organ releases insulin and glucagon?
What happens when cells take up more glucose after insulin?
expected answer: Raised blood glucose tends to fall toward range.
plausible wrong answer: It rises because insulin makes glucose.

hinge question: A simulation uses a single smooth line. Does it predict one person exactly?
plausible wrong answer: Yes; everyone has the same curve.

hinge question: If software is unavailable, can a labelled offline sequence still model the two routes?
expected answer: Yes, if labelled as a model.
plausible wrong answer: No; no learning is possible without a live simulation.
misconception revealed: Confuses tool availability with the concept.

hinge question: Where does blood returning from the body enter?
expected answer: The right side of the heart.
plausible wrong answer: The left side from the lungs.

hinge question: Where does the right side pump blood?
What returns from lungs to the heart?
expected answer: Oxygenated blood to the left side.
plausible wrong answer: Blood directly to body without heart.
misconception revealed: Omits the heart in double circulation.

hinge question: Where does the left side pump blood?
Can blood go body → lungs → body without passing through the heart?
expected answer: No; both circuits pass through the heart.
misconception revealed: Removes the heart from the circuit.

hinge question: Can vessel names be decided from red or blue colour alone?
plausible wrong answer: Yes; colour alone fixes every vessel.
misconception revealed: Uses colour as the sole cue.

hinge question: Why do many alveoli help gas exchange?
expected answer: They provide a large surface area.

hinge question: Why is a thin alveolar wall helpful?
What does blood flow at the exchange surface help maintain?
expected answer: A concentration gradient by carrying gases.
plausible wrong answer: A sealed surface with no exchange.
misconception revealed: Misses the role of supply and removal.

hinge question: What is ventilation?
expected answer: Movement of air in and out of lungs.
misconception revealed: Conflates air movement and gas exchange.

hinge question: If a wall becomes thicker but airflow remains, why can transfer slow?
plausible wrong answer: Normal airflow removes all need for diffusion.
misconception revealed: Treats ventilation as a substitute for diffusion.

hinge question: Would stopped airflow leave the same fresh-air gradient indefinitely?
expected answer: No; the gradient would be harder to maintain.

hinge question: A glucose graph rises then returns toward range. Which principle helps explain it?
misconception revealed: Fails to select the taught principle.

hinge question: Blood goes through lungs and body via the heart. Which model?
Thick alveolar walls can slow transfer because…?
A report gives one number without units or comparison. Can you infer a trend?
expected answer: No; context and units are needed.
plausible wrong answer: Yes; any number proves a trend.

hinge question: Faster breathing alone proves oxygen reached every cell. Is that justified?
expected answer: No; ventilation rose but exchange and circulation evidence is needed.
plausible wrong answer: Yes; breathing rate proves cellular delivery.
misconception revealed: Extends an observation beyond its evidence.

hinge question: What would strengthen an unfamiliar-context claim?
expected answer: A relevant measure, source and limitation.

hinge question: A practice item says “explain”. What must the response do?
expected answer: Give a causal link using the relevant concept.

hinge question: Before interpreting a graph in practice, what do you read?
A practice item names a thick alveolar wall. Which concept applies?
misconception revealed: Does not select the relevant topic.

hinge question: What should a practice response be checked against?
expected answer: The command, evidence and stated concept.

hinge question: Does a practice rehearsal supply answers in the live Paper 2 assessment?
expected answer: No; live assessment follows permitted access arrangements.
plausible wrong answer: Yes; use the model answer in the test.
misconception revealed: Transfers rehearsal support into an assessed response.

hinge question: Why is “alveoli are in lungs” incomplete for “why does a thick wall slow transfer”?
expected answer: It does not link wall thickness to diffusion distance.
plausible wrong answer: It already explains the cause fully.
misconception revealed: Accepts a location fact as a causal explanation.
